issue_context.title: [Feature]Component testing: reuse the same vite server and same vite config file
issue_context.body:
Since my application already uses vite server, I wonder if we can use the same vite sever for both local development and component testing.
and It would be great if we can put the component test configuration in the same vite config file.
comments: While we are considering your request, you can already require it from a shared file

#### Why was this issue closed?

Thank you for your involvement. This issue was closed due to limited engagement (upvotes/activity), lack of recent activity, and insufficient actionability. To maintain a manageable database, we prioritize issues based on these factors.

If you disagree with this closure, please open a new issue and reference this one. More support or clarity on its necessity may prompt a review. Your understanding and cooperation are appreciated.

review_comments: I am not sure doing this unconditionally is a good idea, my production config could have steps that are not relevant (destructive) to my testing.

Hi thank you for the reviews!:) Was thinking about that too. Then i thought perhaps missing configuration can even be more destructive and people will probably run a lot quicker into that. Like missing plugins, import aliases and so on _(see related tickets)_. It might also be better to keep the build config as close as possible to the real build configuration by default unless that causes problems. Then it's possible to override the `vite.config.ts` by defining it in `playwright.config.ts`. 

Vitest and Cypress also use the `vite.config.ts` if it exists. However it's only possible to define/use the config in one place. If the config is put their own config file, the `vite.config.ts` will be ignored. Perhaps that's a better option than working with overrides like i've done now?

> Then i thought perhaps missing configuration can even be more destructive and people will probably run a lot quicker into that. Like missing plugins, import aliases and so on (see related tickets).

They way I think about it is as follows:
- We build components using vite under the hood. It is an implementation detail of Playwright component testing story. Users could be using vite 3 with 3-specific config and we will be using Vite 4, and vice versa. Or they will be using non-vite altogether. We can't force users to bump their vite version and we can't be dependent on their vite version.
- Now that we've established this baseline, we start working on the optimizations that improve our ability to work out of the box. It means that we should now be able to cherry-pick important bits of the configuration from the existing configs. So we should respect babel/webpack aliases, cherry pick bits from vite config, etc. And while doing so, we should be mindful that the user can have any bundler. That's why I think that while bulk-importing production vite config brings up closer to the vite user, conceptually, that's not how we want to organize better support for the existing configuration of the generic user.

In the light of the above, this whole ctViteConfig is a layering violation that was used to jump-start non-trivial amount of the users that could benefit from it immediately. But overall, we should be able to jump the bundler ship and allow users to do so.

Thank you for the explanation! I get your point. I'm still a bit concerned about having a separate bundler and config for test and for prod. For example, what if a Webpack plugin is used which is not supported in Vite? What if the tests are passing while prod is broken because of the difference in bundler and config? I have not encountered this yet and i think time will tell if this is a real problem. Will close the PR.
